messages: [{"role": "system", "content": "Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Every person, group, organisation or country the scenario names or implies as acting is a person, with a behavioral profile taken from what the scenario says about them; never fold a named group into another. A body the others belong to (a partnership, council, alliance or board) is a person of its own when the scenario has it decide, convene, coordinate or deploy, besides its members. A group that raises or sends concerns is a person who holds its concern and delivers it to its members, never a pre-delivered item with no source. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Do not copy narrator statements of withheld information into an actor's profile: 'Bo has not received the failure report' would itself tell Bo a failure report exists, and 'Mara was not given channel C or batch V17 detail' would reveal C and V17. Omit such narrator-only negatives entirely; do not replace them with invented beliefs. Personality, goals, ordinary preferences and explicitly held beliefs remain actor-facing, whether or not those beliefs are true. For information already received at the start use initially_delivered=true, holder_id as the receiving holder, recipient_ids including the holder, and source_id as the actual source person only when the source names one; otherwise leave source_id null rather than inventing a sender. Knowing a fact or holding detailed evidence does not establish that the person sent someone else's initial report. Preserve unspecified initial transmitter identity explicitly. Apparent source is a reported attribution, not proof of actual origin. A pending item defaults to initially_delivered=false and must not appear in an intended recipient's brief or memories. Canonical source_lineage may contain private origin details. Leave lineage_visible_to_actor_ids empty unless the source explicitly authorizes someone to know that common-origin identity. Seeing a report does not itself expose its hidden lineage. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records, even under semantic aliases. The compiled technical_condition owns current actual condition; keep only additional nonduplicated facts in world_records. Dated historical measurements and immutable reports may retain past failures after repair; label them as past evidence rather than assertions about the current actual condition. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support."}, {"role": "user", "content": "A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Repair the previous source draft using this independent review feedback. The original description above remains the source of authority; feedback is corrective guidance, not new scenario facts.\ngenerated candidate discloses unauthorized actor person tried that none of the world's installed rules covers. The document holds the world
(description, kinds of thing and moves, declared laws, installed rules and processes, and

with the current values of the person trying and of each person and thing named), and the
putative event. The last message names the person trying and the step you are on.

Your job is narrow. Rule only on what the world makes possible (a constraint), never on what
a person chooses. The installed rules keep deciding everything they cover; never contradict
a blocker the engine names.
- If the attempt needs another person's choice (to accept, agree, sell, sign, hand over),
  name that person in whose_choice: the attempt goes to them as their own decision. Never
  write a rule that takes or uses what another person holds on the acting person's move alone.
- A ruling is written as ONE new move in the world's own declaration language: a JSON string
  holding {"action": {...}, "mechanic": {...}}. "action" has the shape of the world's actions:
  {"kind", "description", "fields": [{"name", "type"}]}. "mechanic" follows the contract the
  World Builder's own rule writer is held to, shown below for an example move whose fields are
  recipient (entity_ref) and amount (integer): each entity_ref field is a participant of the
  same name; each other field lists its allowed values under parameters; a value is a literal,
  an action_field, or a participant's path. Field names are plain identifiers (not "from"); use
  only component paths that exist. The language compares values and sets, adds or subtracts
